correctness.rationale: The two products separate iff they differ on at least one start state; their actions are x^a y^b and y^b x^a in a right action. All pairs of powers commute iff the two subgroups generated by those powers centralize each other. H_t(m) is normal and is trivial exactly when every cycle length at most m divides t. For m≥5 any nontrivial normal subgroup contains A_m: if its intersection with A_m is trivial it centralizes A_m, and a centralizer element must preserve every support of a three-cycle and so fix every point. Two subgroups containing A_m cannot centralize each other. In degree 3 the power subgroups are S_3, A_3, 1 for d(t)=2,3,≥4. In degree 4 they are S_4, A_4, V_4, 1 for d(t)=2,3,4,≥5; odd powers include transpositions, d=3 powers include 3-cycles which generate A_4, and d=4 powers of 4-cycles give the three double transpositions. In degree 3 the nontrivial centralizing pair is (A_3,A_3); in degree 4 it is (V_4,V_4), as a 3-cycle conjugates the double transpositions nontrivially. S_1 and S_2 already commute. This yields the three corrections in the minimum formula. A least nondivisor must be a prime power because its smaller primary factors would otherwise all divide t. The pairs (1,1) and (2,2) realize 3 and 4, and choosing both exponents as lcm(1,...,q-1) realizes any prime power q≥5.
residual_risks: The reproduction samples exponent pairs and does not prove the all-exponent statement; the group argument supplies it. The result is not for arbitrary binary DFAs.
